title: UI / UX Design Readiness
description: Assess your understanding of user research, usability heuristics, Figma design systems, visual hierarchy, typography, and accessibility.

questions.question: According to Jakob Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics, what does 'Visibility of System Status' mean?
options: The system should always keep users informed about what is going on through timely, appropriate visual feedback (e.g. progress bars, loaders)
The system must show server CPU and memory usage to users
The source code of the application should be public
All database tables should be viewable by all users
questions.explanation: Clear feedback (spinners, checkmarks, progress bars) ensures users always understand the result of their actions and current system state.

questions.question: What is the WCAG 2.1 Level AA minimum contrast ratio requirement for normal text against its background?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.1 AA requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for standard body text and 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold).

questions.question: In Figma, what feature enables components to dynamically expand or contract based on their inner content and padding rules?
options: Auto-Layout
Smart Animate
Vector Network
Boolean Groups
questions.explanation: Auto-Layout applies CSS Flexbox-like behavior to frames, allowing buttons, lists, and cards to resize automatically when content changes.

questions.question: What is Hick's Law in user experience design?
options: The time it takes to make a decision increases logarithmically with the number and complexity of choices presented
Users spend most of their time on other websites, so your site should follow common conventions
The time to acquire a target is a function of target distance and width
People remember the first and last items in a list best
questions.explanation: Hick's Law shows that minimizing options (e.g. simplified menus, focused forms) speeds up decision making and reduces cognitive load.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Wireframe and a Prototype?
options: A wireframe is a static low-fidelity blueprint showing layout and content structure; a prototype is an interactive simulation demonstrating user flows
Wireframes are drawn in code; prototypes are drawn on paper
Prototypes only contain text without images
Wireframes are only created after the product is coded
questions.explanation: Wireframes define structural information architecture, while prototypes add clickability and transitions to test realistic user journeys.

questions.question: What is 'Information Architecture' (IA) in digital product design?
options: The structural organization, hierarchy, labeling, and navigation of content within a digital product to help users find information easily
The physical architecture of database server racks
The choice of frontend JavaScript frameworks
The color grading applied to product photography
questions.explanation: IA focuses on organizing and labeling websites and apps so users intuitively understand where they are and how to find information.

questions.question: In typography, what is 'Kerning'?
options: Adjusting the spacing between specific pairs of individual characters to achieve a visually pleasing result
The vertical distance between baselines of consecutive lines of text (line-height)
The uniform spacing across an entire block of text (tracking)
The thickness or stroke weight of a font
questions.explanation: Kerning adjusts spacing between individual letter pairs (e.g. 'AV' or 'To') to compensate for character geometry.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a 'Card Sorting' user research study?
options: To evaluate and design intuitive information architecture and navigation categorization based on user mental models
To test credit card payment processing speed
To rank user interface mockups by aesthetic beauty
To test keyboard shortcut response times
questions.explanation: Card sorting asks participants to organize topics into categories that make sense to them, guiding menu and taxonomy design.

questions.question: What is Fitts's Law in UI/UX interaction design?
options: The time required to rapidly move to a target area is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target
UI elements should always be designed with flat colors
Users read digital screens in an F-shaped pattern
Mobile screens should have maximum 5 icons per row
questions.explanation: Fitts's Law dictates that interactive targets (like CTAs and buttons) should be large enough and positioned within easy reach (e.g. mobile thumb zone).

questions.question: What are 'Design Tokens' in a design system?
options: The single source of truth for design decisions (colors, spacing, typography, radii) stored as platform-agnostic key-value pairs (JSON/YAML)
Cryptocurrency tokens used to buy UI templates
Physical cards given to participants in user testing
API authentication tokens for Figma plugins
questions.explanation: Design tokens store design values (e.g. `color.primary.500: #3b82f6`) that sync seamlessly between Figma variables and codebases across web and mobile.
